title: Module 8 quiz — JVM Troubleshooting
description: Eight questions on dumps, histograms, CPU, leaks, GC, pools, and container OOM. Method over lucky labels. Synthetic BayPay canary.

questions.prompt: A thread dump shows 180 threads RUNNABLE in the same application frame on pay-prod-east-2. What is the next honest sentence?
choices: Those threads are on-CPU (or want CPU) in that frame; confirm with CPU metrics before calling it a leak
It is a deadlock because RUNNABLE means blocked
questions.explanation: RUNNABLE is the CPU-saturation shape. Deadlock is BLOCKED/WAITING with a cycle. Always pair the dump with instance CPU.

questions.prompt: A heap histogram is dominated by one application type and old-gen used only goes up after each traffic burst. What is established?
choices: A leak candidate: growth + a live type. You still need the retention path
questions.explanation: Histogram + monotonic old-gen is a candidate. Dominators / who holds the map finish the story.

questions.prompt: Found one Java-level deadlock in jstack. Tomcat still has free threads. What should you not do first?
choices: Capture the dump and stop the job that owns one side of the cycle
Bounce Postgres and the entire cell because money is involved
State the two locks and the two owners
Keep Pay-prod-east-1 in rotation if it is not in the cycle
questions.explanation: Deadlock is a JVM lock cycle. The database and WAS DMGR are the wrong blast radius unless evidence says so.

questions.prompt: HTTP threads are 200/200 WAITING. Hikari is 4/50 idle. What have you proven?
choices: The HTTP pool is exhausted; the waiter target is not the JDBC pool
questions.explanation: Thread-pool exhaustion is a symptom. The dump must name what they wait on (downstream, executor, lock) — not assume JDBC.

questions.prompt: GC logs show very high allocation and short-lived String/char[] in the histogram. Old gen is stable. Best first hypothesis class?
choices: Allocation storm (logging or toString on a hot path), not a retained-set leak
questions.explanation: Ephemeral chatter + allocation rate + stable old gen is a GC/pause story. A leak holds objects.

questions.prompt: The pod is OOMKilled. There is no java.lang.OutOfMemoryError: Java heap space in the last log. Flags show -Xmx equal to the 512Mi limit. What is the working model?
choices: cgroup killed the process because RSS (heap + native + stacks) exceeded the limit
questions.explanation: Container OOM ≠ heap OOME. Equal Xmx and limit is the classic setup. Fix headroom, not ‘more GC.’

questions.prompt: Why does a lucky one-word label (‘leak’) fail Diagnostic method even if it later matches the solution file?
choices: The rubric forbids the word leak
The score rewards gated evidence and an updatable hypothesis, not a guessed noun
Only Staff engineers may say leak
questions.explanation: Same rule as Modules 2, 4, and 5. Method is 20%. A noun without gates is a guess.

questions.prompt: east-1 is healthy, east-2 canary is on fire after 3.8.x. Default stabilize?
choices: Take east-2 out of rotation or revert the canary; leave the healthy replica serving Avery Chen
Set -Xmx to the container limit on both
questions.explanation: Canary isolation is the point of east-2. Do not widen to the WAS cell or the healthy Boot replica.
